data.title: Michael Burry Sounds Alarm on Nvidia's $500B AI Funding Plan: What Went Wrong?
data.description:
The Big Short investor Michael Burry has questioned the progress of a massive $500 billion financing plan tied to Nvidia (NVDA). Despite earlier pledges from some of Wall Street's biggest financial firms, no capital has been deployed so far.

In a post on X on Thursday, Burry shared a report by The Wall Street Journal highlighting delays in the plan, which was first discussed in August. The initiative aims to help Nvidia customers finance AI chip purchases as demand for computing power grows.

Wall Street Giants Have Yet to Put Money to Work

The financing plan involves six major financial firms: Apollo Global Management (APO), Blackstone (BX), BlackRock (BLK), Brookfield Asset Management (BAM), Goldman Sachs (GS), and KKR (KKR).

The firms had agreed to explore ways to raise as much as $500 billion to fund AI chip purchases and related projects. However, their initial commitments were made through a nonbinding memorandum of understanding, meaning they were not legally bound to raise a set amount.

The plan was driven by Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang's efforts to expand funding options for customers building AI data centers. However, talks have faced hurdles over Nvidia's proposed credit guarantees, which could cover up to 25% of project costs.

Lenders are seeking stronger protections before moving ahead. Talks on the first chip-backed financing deal are ongoing, but an agreement is not expected before 2027, according to the report.

Burry Maintains Bearish Bet on NVDA

Burry has maintained his bearish position on Nvidia, holding $140 strike put options expiring in February 2027. Ahead of Nvidia's latest earnings, he ruled out buying short-term call options to hedge against a possible rally, saying, "I am not buying calls, no."

He also noted that retail buying could lift Nvidia shares in the short term, but remains cautious about the longer-term outlook. Beyond his direct Nvidia puts, Burry has bearish exposure through put options on the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the Nasdaq-100 index (NDX).

Burry has also raised concerns about Huang's departure, arguing that Nvidia's grip on the AI supply chain could weaken without its longtime CEO. He believes customers and business partners may have more room to renegotiate deals, delay purchases or turn to competitors, potentially slowing growth and putting pressure on profit margins.

Separately, Burry drew attention to Nvidia's delayed Form 10-Q filing, adding another point of scrutiny around the company.

Is Nvidia a Strong Buy?

On TipRanks, NVDA has a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell rating. The average Nvidia price target of $232.59 implies 54.1% upside potential from current levels.

data.title: Anthropic IPO: Claude Maker Prepares for Biggest IPO in History at $1.5 Trillion Valuation
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) is set to make history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record. The company behind the Claude AI chatbot priced its shares at $83 each, above its initial range. The IPO values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Anthropic is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq (NDAQ) on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT.

The company raised $81.3 billion through the sale of 980 million shares. It is also raising another $26 billion through a private placement, taking the total deal size to $107.3 billion. This puts Anthropic ahead of SpaceX (SPCX), which had set the prior record with its IPO.

Strong Demand Drives Record IPO

The IPO was six times oversubscribed, helping Anthropic price its shares above the top end of its first range. The company had first planned to sell shares at $70 to $78 each, which would have valued it at about $1.4 trillion.

The record IPO comes amid growing concerns about the high cost of AI development and the large sums tech firms are spending on chips and data centers. Anthropic's public debut will give investors a chance to assess the value of a major AI model maker in the public market.

Claude Growth Drives Revenue Higher

Demand for Claude and Claude Code, Anthropic's AI tool for software developers, has helped drive rapid business growth.

Anthropic's third-quarter revenue reached $17 billion, up 47% from the prior quarter and more than 12 times higher than a year earlier. Its annualized revenue run rate (not reported annual revenue) reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30.

The company also reported 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue as of September 30. This compares with more than 1,500 such customers at the end of last year.

High Computing Costs Remain a Key Risk

Despite strong growth, Anthropic faces high costs as it builds and runs its AI systems. The company spent nearly $9 billion on computing and infrastructure in the first half of 2026. It also reported an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter, compared with operating income of $974 million in the prior quarter.

Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in future computing commitments with partners, including Amazon (AMZN) and Google (GOOGL). These costs will be important to watch as the company expands its AI services.

What Is the Forecast for ANT Stock?

Currently, three research firms have initiated coverage of ANT stock with Buy ratings and bullish price targets. Needham analyst Scott Berg set a $150 target, while New Street Research's five-star analyst Pierre Ferragu set a $105 target. Citizens JMP analyst Patrick Walravens set a $125 target.

Based on the $83 IPO price, these targets point to potential upside of about 81%, 26.5%, and 50.6%, respectively.

data.title: Quantum Computing News: IBM, Nvidia, and AMD Team Up on New Quantum Projects
data.description:
Welcome to Thursday's quantum computing news recap. This edition covers new partnerships involving IBM, Nvidia, and AMD, along with a bigger quantum computing roadmap from Alice & Bob. We also have Infleqtion's latest earnings and a proposed acquisition by SEALSQ that could expand its reach in quantum cybersecurity.

1. Alice & Bob Doubles Its Quantum Computing Target to 200 Logical Qubits

We begin with French quantum computing company Alice & Bob, which unveiled an ambitious new roadmap targeting 200 logical qubits by 2030, double its previous goal. The company plans to reach that milestone using just 3,600 physical cat qubits, which are designed to reduce certain quantum errors directly in the hardware.

The roadmap starts with six logical qubits in 2028, followed by 1,024 in 2032 and 2,048 by 2034. These systems could eventually support applications in materials science, chemistry, and cryptography.

Alice & Bob also plans to connect multiple quantum processors at extremely low temperatures to build larger systems. The company says it has already built and operated three independent processors and demonstrated the key components needed for a logical qubit. The challenge now is turning those early results into working systems at a much larger scale.

2. SEALSQ Plans Acquisition of Quantum Cybersecurity Firm QuintessenceLabs

SEALSQ Corp. (LAES) has signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire 100% of Australian quantum cybersecurity company QuintessenceLabs. The proposed purchase would be funded through a mix of cash and SEALSQ shares, although the companies have not disclosed a deal value.

The acquisition would combine SEALSQ's secure chips and post-quantum security products with QuintessenceLabs' quantum random number generation, encryption key management, and secure communications technologies. The goal is to offer broader security solutions to governments, banks, and businesses preparing for future quantum computing threats.

The companies have entered a 60-day exclusivity period and are targeting completion in the first half of 2027. The deal is not final, and the new shares issued to fund it would dilute existing SEALSQ shareholders.

3. IBM and Nvidia Join Fermilab to Develop Quantum Supercomputing

IBM (IBM), Nvidia (NVDA), and Fermilab announced a collaboration to develop a modular quantum computing platform for scientific research.

The project will combine IBM's quantum processors, Nvidia's accelerated computing technology, and Fermilab's expertise in superconducting hardware. Researchers plan to focus on complex problems in particle physics, nuclear science, and neutrino research.

One goal is to connect quantum computers with conventional supercomputing systems, allowing researchers to use both technologies in the same workflow. Fermilab also plans to contribute superconducting cavity technology that could help store quantum information and reduce errors.

The collaboration remains a research effort rather than a commercial product launch, but it could help researchers design quantum systems around real scientific problems.

4. Infleqtion Revenue Climbs 57% as Quantum Technology Advances

Quantum computing company Infleqtion (INFQ) reported $32.6 million in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, up 57% from a year earlier. Third-quarter revenue reached $9.1 million, a 25% increase.

The growth came alongside rising costs. Infleqtion's third-quarter operating loss widened to $34.5 million from $6.7 million a year ago, showing how expensive developing quantum technology remains.

On the technology side, Infleqtion demonstrated 30 entangled logical qubits using 80 physical qubits on its Sqale system. The company says AI helped cut the number of physical gates needed for a key operation by half.

Infleqtion is now targeting 100 logical qubits by 2028. It also secured a $20 million NASA contract expansion for quantum gravity sensing technology, adding to its growing work with government customers.

5. AMD and IQM Demonstrate Hybrid Quantum Computing for Chemistry

We end with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and IQM Quantum Computers (IQMX), which demonstrated a hybrid computing system that combines quantum processors with conventional GPUs to solve chemistry problems.

The project used IQM's 20-qubit Garnet processor alongside AMD Instinct GPUs to calculate the energy of hydrogen molecules. Researchers tested the system across 17 different molecular bond lengths, showing that the two computing technologies could work together.

The partners also released the workflow as an open-source Jupyter notebook, allowing developers to explore the approach. The test did not demonstrate that quantum computers outperform classical systems. Instead, it showed that quantum hardware and AMD's GPU software can work together in a complete computing process.

The companies now plan to explore more complex molecules and tighter connections between the two systems, with the goal of making hybrid quantum computing more useful for scientific research.

data.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 19: Anthropic's $81 Billion IPO Takes Center Stage
data.description:
U.S. stock futures moved higher ahead of Thursday's opening bell as investors focused on Anthropic's (ANT) highly anticipated Nasdaq debut. The maker of Claude AI is targeting a potential $1.5 trillion valuation, making it one of the largest IPOs in history.

Futures on the Nasdaq-100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were up 2.07%, 1.16%, and 0.57%, respectively, as of 5:40 a.m. EST on November 19.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its initial target range of $70 to $78, following strong investor demand. The company also increased the offering size from 825 million to 980 million shares. The IPO is expected to raise approximately $81.34 billion, surpassing SpaceX's (SPCX) $75 billion June offering to become the largest IPO on record. The company is also raising an additional $26 billion through a private placement.

Meanwhile, oil prices edged higher on Thursday after falling in the previous session. Concerns about rising global oil supply and higher U.S. interest rates limited gains, while renewed geopolitical risks in the Middle East supported prices. Reports of possible further U.S. action against Iran and attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz also kept supply concerns in focus.

At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, rose 0.76% to $92.65 per barrel, while WTI crude futures rose 0.65% to $83.80 per barrel.

During Wednesday's regular trading session, the three major U.S. indexes closed mixed. The DJIA fell 1.11%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.23%, marking its fifth straight day of losses. The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.42%.

Looking ahead, investors will also watch data on weekly jobless claims for further clues about the strength of the U.S. labor market. On the earnings front, results from Walmart (WMT), Alibaba (BABA), and Gap (GAP) are scheduled for release today. 

Global Markets

European markets traded mixed on Thursday, while Asia-Pacific markets closed mostly lower. Investors remained cautious ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, as concerns about AI valuations and the outlook for U.S. interest rates continued to weigh on sentiment.

Investors also kept an eye on the trilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The talks could focus on nuclear arms control, the Ukraine war, and global security. Any progress could ease geopolitical tensions and improve investor sentiment.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index dropped 1.95%. In China, the Shanghai Composite fell 0.28%, and the Shenzhen Component was down 1.20%. The Nikkei 225 added 0.71% and the Topix declined 0.04%.

data.title: Morgan Stanley Says AI Has a Labor Problem — and These 2 'Strong Buy' Stocks Could Cash In
data.description:
Despite recent setbacks, including the scandal surrounding Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, growing concerns over excessive AI spending, and political uncertainty following the midterm elections, AI remains a key growth driver. However, the opportunities extend beyond chip giants, cloud computing providers, and software developers, with companies responsible for building the infrastructure needed to support AI also positioned to benefit.

Morgan Stanley analyst Stephan Diaz sees considerable potential in the Engineering and Construction (E&C) sector, where demand for skilled workers is outpacing supply. As AI infrastructure projects become larger and more complex, companies with established workforces and specialized expertise could gain a competitive advantage. Diaz believes this labor shortage could translate into stronger growth for leading E&C companies.

"Large Engineering and Construction (E&C) companies have established positions in one of the infrastructure buildout's key bottlenecks: skilled labor. The training and experience required to develop crews make that capacity difficult to replicate quickly. Most operate in highly specialized verticals such as high and low voltage electric, HVAC, plumbing, and civil. To help safeguard the skilled labor advantage companies in our coverage own, operate, and implement schools, training programs, and staffing companies. Alongside national footprints and strong balance sheets, this supports outsized growth in a narrowly growing non-residential construction market driven by share gains as projects continue to skew larger, more remote, and more complex," Diaz explained.

With this opportunity in mind, Diaz has highlighted two E&C stocks that could benefit from the growing demand for AI infrastructure. Using the TipRanks database, we've taken a closer look at two of his picks, both of which carry Strong Buy consensus ratings from Wall Street. Here's what makes these companies worth watching.

Comfort Systems USA (FIX)

The first stock we'll look at, Comfort Systems USA, is a mechanical and electrical contract service provider, based in Houston, Texas. The company is a member of the S&P 500 index and has been since December of last year. Comfort Systems is a holding company with a network of 50-plus operating companies that provide services across 184 locations in the US. The engineering services provided include building and support for mechanical, electrical, modular, and plumbing building systems – the systems necessary to put empty building shells into operation.

Comfort Systems operates through two segments: Mechanical, which covers HVAC, plumbing, process piping, modular and off-site construction, fire protection, and building automation; and Electrical, which includes installation, servicing, and system integration. Its services also span the building lifecycle, including new construction, ongoing maintenance, retrofits, and renovations.

The stock has been volatile this year due to swinging sentiment in the AI sector – it peaked above $2,000 in the summer, and is down 41% in the past six months – but even with that, FIX shares are still up some 18% for the year-to-date.

Looking at the company's most recent set of financials, we find that Comfort Systems reported $3.77 billion in revenue for 3Q26, up more than 53% year-over-year and more than $365 million better than had been expected. The diluted EPS of $13.91 beat the forecast by $1.06. The company's outlook is also supported by its growing order backlog, which reached $17.81 billion at the end of Q3, up almost 90% year-over-year.

Morgan Stanley's Diaz starts with that backlog in his discussion of Comfort Systems and from there he looks at the stock's prospects in the coming year, writing, "Current backlog levels suggest growth above and beyond our own forecasts when assuming historical conversion rates hold, suggesting opportunity for positive earnings revisions. In addition, strong hyperscaler capex growth, where MS is ahead of street estimates, and a differentiated modular business where FIX has guided to 50% capacity growth in 2027 supports this sentiment. Moreover, the recent de-rating in shares has made for an attractive entry point for a company that recently posted accelerating bookings, guided 2027 to mid-twenties revenue growth, and has the ability to expand its modular offering beyond guided levels due to its net cash position and given current capacity investment plans are with current customers only (mainly 2 hyperscalers)."

Quantifying this stance, Diaz puts an Overweight (i.e., Buy) rating on the stock, along with a $1,410 price target that implies a one-year upside potential of ~24%. (To watch Diaz's track record, click here)

Wall Street is even more bullish, with the average price target of $1,849 suggesting shares could surge 62% from current levels. All eight recent analyst ratings are Buys, giving FIX stock a unanimous Strong Buy consensus rating. (See FIX stock forecast)

EMCOR Group (EME)

EMCOR, the next stock we'll look at, is another multi-billion-dollar player in the US construction industry. The company traces its business roots back to 1966, but has been operating in its current incarnation since 1994. EMCOR offers construction services, building services, and industrial services – three core divisions that together make up a vital chunk of the Construction and Engineering segment.

Through its construction services, EMCOR builds and maintains power systems, data centers, and semiconductor plants, and provides them with HVAC installations, fire protection, and modern industrial piping. The building services segment overlaps with HVAC and plumbing, and also includes energy solutions and facility management. Finally, industrial services include work involving refineries, carbon capture, water treatment, and other vital infrastructure. EMCOR works with customers in both the commercial and government sectors.

EMCOR works through a network of about 100 subsidiary operating companies. This network has well over 400 locations across the US, and generated $16.99 billion in revenues last year. And, to build out the array of services it provides, EMCOR has over 47,000 skilled-labor employees, bringing skill and expertise to the ambitious construction projects.

Earlier this month, EMCOR revealed that it has entered an agreement to acquire P1 Construction, a mechanical and electrical contractor serving high-growth markets in the Midwest. The deal was announced as an all-cash transaction, but exact terms were not released.

The last quarterly report covered 3Q26, and showed strong gains from 3Q25. Revenue was up almost 29% year-over-year, and hit $5.54 billion. Earnings were up 46.1%; the non-GAAP EPS of $9.60 beat the forecast by $1.24 per share. And, like Comfort Systems above, EMCOR has a strong work backlog – it reported remaining performance obligations of $18.57 billion at the end of Q3, for a 47.2% year-over-year jump.

All of this explains why analyst Diaz is bullish here. In his coverage for Morgan Stanley, he states, "With a history of solid execution, current backlog levels suggest upside to consensus estimates in 2027, and an undemanding valuation, we view the set-up favorable for EME. Data center work is also a growing share of that backlog, which in the current macro environment will likely be met with question marks. That said, EME's data center exposure is ~70%/30% cloud vs. AI which should help sentiment. In addition, we find EME's M&A strategy particularly attractive as the company has shown it can pay below public company multiples for contractors without material data center exposure and then layer its own data center pipeline on top, effectively acquiring skilled craft labor, the industry's main bottleneck, at a discount to its own multiple. We view EME as a lower beta way to gain exposure to the AI infrastructure demand cycle given its exposure to union labor, more diversified end markets and lower fixed investment risk to data centers vs. FIX."

Reflecting his confidence, Diaz rates EME as Overweight (i.e., Buy), with a $799 price target suggesting shares could climb ~24% over the next 12 months.

The rest of the Street shares that positive outlook, with 6 Buys and 2 Holds giving EME a Strong Buy consensus rating. At its current price of $644.17, the stock offers a 31.5% potential upside, based on the average analyst target of $849.71. (See EME stock forecast)

data.title: Intel Stock (INTC) Rises on First External Advanced 18A Chip Customer Win
data.description:
Intel (INTC) stock rose in Thursday's premarket trading after CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the chipmaker has signed its first external customer for its 18A chips as it gears up to compete with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM), or TSMC, CNBC reported. Tan made the statement at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas. Pushkar Ranade, Intel's technology chief, clarified on X that the external customer had signed up for Intel's 18A-P manufacturing process node, which went into risk production in June.

Additionally, Tan announced that Microsoft (MSFT) is its first publicly named customer for its most advanced packaging technology, called EMIB (Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge).

Intel Makes Efforts to Turn Around Chip Business

The first external customer win for the advanced 18A chips marks a key milestone for Intel, which is trying to turn around its business and compete with TSMC, a market leader in chip manufacturing. After years of missteps, product delays, and market share losses to rivals like Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), the company is focusing on innovation under Tan's leadership. Intel's turnaround is also being supported by the U.S. government, which took a 10% stake in the company in August 2025. Moreover, semiconductor giant Nvidia (NVDA) invested $5 billion in Intel last year.

Intel believes that its 18A offering is vital to support its efforts to emerge as a competitive chipmaker. While the company didn't provide details about the external customer, reports in May indicated that Apple (AAPL) and Intel were nearing a deal for Intel to produce some chips for Apple devices.

Intel stock has declined 39% over the past month due to weak guidance, AI trade concerns, and broader market pressures, but is still up 48% year-to-date. Last month, the company issued lower-than-expected fourth-quarter guidance, citing persistent weakness in the PC market.

However, AI-led demand for advanced CPUs is expected to drive the company's sales higher in the times ahead. Tan recently said he expects the global server processors market to grow fivefold over the next five years to about $200 billion, though he said that Intel is not currently in a position to meet the massive customer demand. Until now, the company didn't have a major outside customer for its foundry business, which manufactures chips for its own products at its factories, including a massive new campus in Arizona.

Is INTC a Good Stock to Buy Now?

Currently, Wall Street has a Hold consensus rating on Intel stock based on 25 Holds, seven Buys, and one Sell. Several analysts are cautious as they await continued improvement in the company's financials and solid execution. The average INTC stock price target of $90.93 indicates 66.3% upside potential.

data.title: Nvidia Courts Arm CEO Rene Haas to Replace Jensen Huang
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) has approached Arm (ARM) CEO Rene Haas as a possible replacement for Jensen Huang, according to Bloomberg. The chipmaker has yet to make a formal offer, and Haas has not accepted the role. Nvidia continues its search for a permanent candidate, with Colette Kress currently serving as interim CEO.

The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Nvidia hired Heidrick & Struggles to find its next CEO. The firm has reportedly spoken with potential candidates, including Haas.

Haas Background at Nvidia

Haas spent seven years at Nvidia, from 2006 to 2013, rising to vice president and general manager of computing products. He joined Arm in 2013 and became its CEO in February 2022. Nvidia also tried to acquire Arm in 2020, but the deal fell through amid regulatory opposition.

Speaking at a tech conference in Austin on Wednesday, Haas described his former boss as "a legend." "What he built at Nvidia is historic; you don't have many champions like that," Haas said.

Other potential candidates include Nvidia Vice President Ian Buck, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) CEO Lisa Su, and Apple (AAPL) Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji. President Donald Trump has also floated the idea of former Apple CEO Tim Cook taking the job.

Nvidia Without Huang

Nvidia cut ties with Huang on November 12 after revelations about his extramarital affairs triggered a widening scandal. Huang has admitted to a relationship with a woman who has been investigated by the U.S. government over alleged spying for China.

Huang led Nvidia for more than 30 years. The company wants to show investors it can keep growing without Huang. Nvidia also held a meeting with employees on Wednesday. Interim CEO Colette Kress sought to reassure staff with a simple message: "We've got this."

Nvidia is also pointing to its strong financial performance. In Q3 FY27, EPS came in at $2.68, beating estimates of $2.48. Revenue surged 103% year-over-year to $115.8 billion, topping expectations of $108.97 billion. Data Center revenue jumped 110% to $107.6 billion, accounting for about 93% of total sales.

Is NVDA Stock a Buy?

Nvidia's stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell issued in the past three months. The average NVDA price target of $232.59 implies 54% upside from current levels.
